statement: Combined FY2027 capex of the 5 largest AI/cloud spenders >= 1.2x FY2026 (on FY2027 filings)
status_at_phase_end: FY2026 base forming: big-four calendar-2026 guidance ~USD 720-740bn after Q3 reports (all Bloc A firms); two of the five explicitly guided 2027 'significantly'/'meaningfully' higher; sell-side forecasts ~+50% for 2027. Cash-flow strain and one guidance trim are counter-signals.

items.summary: Q4-2025 earnings season: the largest spenders guided 2026 capex sharply higher - one ~USD 200bn (vs ~USD 131bn in 2025), another USD 175-185bn (vs USD 91bn), another USD 115-135bn (vs USD 72bn). Analysts raised top-5 2026 estimates to ~USD 750bn (+~67% y/y).

Mid-year guidance raised again: one spender to ~USD 220bn (citing higher memory costs and insufficient capacity), another to USD 195-205bn; the latter said capex would 'increase significantly in 2027'.
items.detail: Alphabet $195-205bn (2026-07-22); Amazon ~$220bn cash capex (2026-07-30); Meta $130-145bn; Microsoft ~$175bn calendar 2026 (2026-07-29). Compiled from company calls via secondary tracker.

items.summary: Q3-2026 filings: one spender's quarterly purchases of property and equipment were USD 51.4bn (+114% y/y) with negative free cash flow (-USD 9.1bn); it held 2026 guidance and again said 2027 capex will rise significantly.
items.detail: Alphabet Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC EDGAR exhibit 99.1).

items.summary: Another top spender trimmed its 2026 capex outlook to ~USD 170bn from ~USD 175bn because third-party GPU capacity was delayed to H1 2027, while saying spending would accelerate in H1 2027. Delay shifts spend into FY2027 rather than reducing it.
items.detail: Microsoft FY27 Q1: $45.2bn capex incl. finance leases (+30% y/y), below $50.7bn consensus; CFO Amy Hood comments (CNBC 2026-10-29).

items.summary: After Q3 reports, the big four guided calendar-2026 capex at ~USD 720-740bn; their Q3 capex was ~USD 208.7bn (+84% y/y). The largest spender (Q3 ~USD 75.9bn) said 2027 spend will be 'meaningfully' higher; a fifth spender guides ~USD 90-95bn gross for its fiscal year to May 2027.
items.detail: Amazon ~$220bn, Alphabet $195-205bn, Microsoft ~$170bn, Meta $135-145bn; Oracle FY27 up to ~$95bn gross / <=$70bn net cash.

items.summary: Sell-side forecast: hyperscaler capex projected at ~USD 1.2tn in 2027 (~+50% y/y) and USD 1.4tn in 2028; consensus ~USD 1.1tn for 2027. Implies a ratio well above the 1.2x threshold if realised.
items.detail: Goldman Sachs research 'AI capex, required revenues, and what's priced in the AI trade' (2026-09-24).

items.summary: Financing strain: several of the five spenders had negative free cash flow, halted buybacks, and issued new equity to fund capex; credit outlook for one was revised to negative. A constraint that could cap 2027 growth.
items.detail: Alphabet ~$50bn new stock in June + $12.4bn ATM; Oracle $19.9bn stock; Meta $22.5bn forward share sale (2026-10-26); S&P outlook on Meta negative. Big-five buybacks $4.4bn in Q3 (Kobeissi tally via Yahoo).
